The Pentagon is delaying the delivery of around 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, including missiles from European arsenals already paid for by Kyiv’s allies.
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to approve the transfers, while a separate agreement allowing Ukraine to manufacture its own Patriot interceptors remains under Pentagon review. 
Ukrainian officials suspect the Trump administration is withholding military assistance to pressure Kyiv into accepting territorial concessions to Russia. 
The Pentagon insists its policy on supporting Ukraine has not changed.

🇪🇸🇮🇱 Spain maintains Israeli military technology in its Armed Forces despite the arms embargo.
Missiles, radars, weapon stations, and electronic warfare equipment from Israeli manufacturers remain integrated into Spanish platforms, according to military sources. An exception clause in the royal decree allows transfers to continue when general interests are at stake.
The government of Pedro Sánchez decreed a ban on the purchase and sale of weapons with Israel and placed the rupture with Benjamin Netanyahu’s administration at the core of its foreign policy. However, the Spanish Armed Forces continue to rely on Israeli technology to operate, maintain, and modernise some of their weapon systems.

events.text:
⚡️🇩🇪🇱🇹 Reuters: Germany's army has begun its first tactical tests of kamikaze drones in Lithuania, along with Helsing's AI based targeting software Clarity. The drone tests took place on Sunday during Freedom Shield, Germany's largest military drills in the country to date.
Army chief Lieutenant General Christian Freuding watched loitering munitions made by German companies Helsing and Stark, fitted with inert warheads, hit main battle tanks at the Rudninkai training ground near the Belarusian border. Days earlier, troops there tested Clarity, which processes data from satellites, drones and other sensors and recommends actions to commanders. Freuding described both kinds of systems as essential to modern warfare.
Germany only decided in 2025 to buy loitering munitions. An armoured brigade of 5,000 German troops will be stationed permanently in Lithuania by the end of 2027, with about 1,800 already deployed there.

👤💵 Nvidia market cap surges $954 billion in a day as Jensen Huang returns as CEO
Nvidia shares skyrocketed 31.48% to $165.05 on Monday, adding roughly $954 billion in market value in a single session—the largest one-day gain in US stock market history.
The company's market capitalization jumped from $3.031 trillion to $3.985 trillion, propelling it back to second place among the world's most valuable companies, behind only Apple at $5.073 trillion.
The rally came after [Nvidia's board reinstated founder Jensen Huang as CEO](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78232), reversing its earlier position that he would not return. Huang had stepped down on November 12 amid a scandal involving extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence.

💵 Iranian courts order US to pay $290 billion for decades of hostile actions
Iranian courts have secured more than $290 billion in judgments against the United States over decades of hostile actions and damage inflicted on Iran, Press TV reported, citing judiciary official Hassan Abdolianpour, the head of the Judiciary’s Center for Lawyers, Official Experts and Family Counselors.
💬 “When we began our activities, we had secured less than $40 billion in judgments against the United States,” Abdolianpour said.
💬 “Today, however, we have secured more than $290 billion in judgments against the United States, some of which have already been enforced.”
During the recent US-Israeli wars, around 19,000 Iranian experts helped assess damage and document alleged crimes. Iran has also compiled statements, tweets and directives by US officials dating back to the 2020 assassination of General Qassem Soleimani for use in legal proceedings.
Abdolianpour said the judgments could lead to further enforcement measures, including potentially examining the seizure of vessels. He linked part of US pressure over reopening the Strait of Hormuz to these rulings.
Iran is also preparing a November 24 hearing over[ the US attack on an elementary school in Minab](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75462), which killed 168 children and teachers. Legal professionals from around five countries representing five continents are expected to attend.

🚀 Iran downs another $35,000 US LUCAS drone over Hormuz
Iran’s Army Air Defense Force shot down a US LUCAS one-way attack drone over the Persian Gulf, east of the Strait of Hormuz, the Army’s public relations office said.
The drone was destroyed by domestically developed Iranian air defense systems operating under the country’s integrated air defense network.
LUCAS is modeled on Iran’s Shahed-136, and each US drone reportedly costs around $35,000.
It is far from the first LUCAS Iran has brought down, with previous US drones of the same type[ intercepted over southern Iran](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76773) and [near the Strait of Hormuz](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77912).

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
👉 THROWBACK: Anduril co-founder boasts of inventing a VR headset designed to kill its user
Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey is not only a vocal proponent of AI-driven autonomous kill chains and a self-described fan of public executions: in 2022 he invented a VR headset that will kill the user if they die in the game they’re playing.
🔴Only the threat of serious consequences can make a game feel real to you," he argued.🔴
Luckey was inspired by the anime Sword Art Online, in which players put on a NerveGear virtual reality headset only to find out that real life is now at stake as their gear was programmed by a mad scientist to kill them if they are killed in a virtual game.
“The good news is that we are halfway to making a true NerveGear. The bad news is that so far, I have only figured out the half that kills you,” Luckey wrote in his blog.
He noted he had plans for an anti-tamper mechanism "that, like the NerveGear, will make it impossible to remove or destroy the headset."
Luckey used small, modular explosive charges and connected them to a light sensor that detects when the headset displays a red screen flashing at a specific frequency.
“When an appropriate game-over screen is displayed, the charges fire, instantly destroying the brain of the user,” he noted. “It is also, as far as I know, the first non-fiction example of a VR device that can actually kill the user. It won’t be the last.”
Some say it's going too far, even for a high-tech provocateur, while others point out that Luckey's Anduril is already producing all kinds of killer drones and other military equipment.
Luckey's provocative rhetoric bears a striking resemblance to that of Alex Karp, co-founder of [Palantir](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68441). Both Anduril and Palantir received financial backing from Peter Thiel, the PayPal Mafia billionaire fascinated by [The Lord of the Rings](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72488).
In Tolkien's mythology, a palantír is a seeing stone, while Anduril is a legendary sword known as the "Flame of the West" and a symbol of legitimate authority.
Both AI giants openly proclaim the "defense of the West" as their core mission, seemingly by any means necessary. Yet their role in creating AI-powered military targeting systems has drawn widespread criticism over ethical concerns, particularly amid mounting civilian casualties in conflicts across the [Middle East and Eastern Europe](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78025). This has fuelled questions about their underlying ideology, with some critics openly labeling them as "techno-fascists."
